hints.title: Shortest Path State Obstacle
hints.text: A pricier path can be the only valid one when a cheaper path uses too many stops, so keeping only the cheapest cost per city throws away valid answers. What extra information does a partial path need to carry?

hints.title: Bounded Edge Count Formulation
hints.text: Track the best cost to each city after each allowed number of flights, so every round adds at most one flight.

hints.title: Layered Edge Relaxation
hints.text: Initialize an array dist of size n with infinity and dist[src] = 0. Repeat for k + 1 rounds: create a copy of dist, and for every directed flight from u to v with price w, update copy[v] to min(copy[v], dist[u] + w) whenever dist[u] is finite. At the end of each round, set dist to copy. Return dist[dst] if reachable, or -1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Bellman-Ford relaxation across at most K + 1 edge rounds.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard Dijkstra only records the cheapest distance to each node, prematurely discarding a pricier path that reaches a node in fewer stops. Backtracking all paths recursively takes exponential O(V^(K+1)) time, which exceeds 100^100 operations and triggers severe Time Limit Exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining two arrays of size O(V) (dist and temp snapshot) prevents cascading updates within a single step and guarantees O(K * E) time across at most K + 1 rounds with O(V) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why a temporary distance snapshot is strictly necessary (to prevent taking multiple flights in a single round); properly returning -1 when destination is unreachable.

solutions.approach: Bounded Edge Count (Bellman-Ford / DP state expansion)
